features.feature: AI & minutes lists the profiles with their kind (Built in, Claude account, Model on a host, Wrapper), "Default for new calls", minutes and live models; Make default changes it
With several profiles the minutes and the Live tab offer a profile picker; with one they don't; the Record button never does (the account chip picks the default)
A call keeps the profile it was recorded with; changing the default later never moves it
A job whose profile is missing, unreadable, signed out or on another account fails with the reason, never on another profile
A Claude profile signs in from the window (Sign in…, Cancel), the tray or `echoctl ai login`; "Signed in as …"; another account asks "Use X"

Admin policy that could route Claude Code or switch hooks off refuses the runs it would affect; a policy file Echo can't read asks (#404): a profile's own file offers Claude Code (as configured), a managed file only the admin may read offers to write anyway, a broken managed one says Claude Code won't start with it
`echoctl ai status / add-local / add-claude / add-wrapper / update-wrapper / default / remove` manage profiles as the window shows them

A minutes model Claude Code can't use fails with what's wrong and where to change it (the menu and `echoctl ai set`); a run the model answered in that fails later says its own error, never "can't use the model"

The account chip at the top bar's right end, left of the Inbox, shows the default profile by name (tooltip: its account and where it runs); with several profiles its menu drops below it — each profile its name and one line (model, then its account's address or where it runs), the default checked, and Manage profiles… (Settings → AI & minutes) at its foot — and picks the default as Make default does (kept, the status bar and Settings follow), with one it opens the Claude session (as the status bar's Claude), with none it is gone

A local profile whose Ollama server gives its minutes or live-notes model less than 64k tokens of context is warned about, with OLLAMA_CONTEXT_LENGTH: `echoctl doctor` loads the model to check (not with `--no-ai`, `--request`, `--probe`, `--open`), `echoctl ai status` only reads what is loaded; an Ollama that doesn't report the context says so; a server without /api/ps is never warned about or sent a load

A wrapper profile (`echoctl ai add-wrapper`) starts a program the user installed in place of `claude`, on their own setup: added only when it resolves (a name as the login shell finds it, links followed) outside Echo's data and own folders and answers `--version` as Claude Code, never from inside a run; `ai status` shows its command; a program gone fails its jobs saying so

A run through a wrapper gets its text only on stdin once its own settings' session-start hook answered with the run's value; Echo's gate holds every tool call until Echo checked the run's start event (Claude Code new enough, the permission mode, tools and MCP servers Echo set); a start that doesn't match, or no answer within 90 s, stops it saying why and naming the wrapper
On a wrapper profile the window's folder and call sessions start with Echo's proof hooks; the call session's first prompt is typed in after the hook answered, never on its command line

AI & minutes adds a wrapper typed in (Add a wrapper…): Check shows where the login shell finds it and its version (what an older Claude Code lacks too), or why it can't be one, before Add profile; a wrapper profile's row says what it starts and that it sees and can change everything Echo sends to Claude, call transcripts included

A plugin's `uses.ai.wrapper` is a line on its sheet and an offer in AI & minutes (Offered by …, Add…), added only by the user (window or `ai add-wrapper --plugin`); an update naming another program asks again and is said on the profile, taken only by Use it (`ai update-wrapper`); the plugin switched off or removed leaves the profile; a same-id plugin from another marketplace offers nothing to it

Inside a run Echo started, a wrapper profile is never made the default, a call's or a thread's or the next recording's (`ai default`, a call's profile, `project set --profile`, `arm --ai` or a meeting file's, `memo start --ai`); a plugin's job (`ctx.claude.run({profile})`) runs on one only when it is the user's default

Each AI profile but the built-in one maps Claude's names (haiku, sonnet, opus) to its provider's own models: set by the user in AI & minutes (Models… on its row; the row says what each runs) or `ai set <id> --model <name>=<model>` (empty clears; all checked before any is saved; refused inside a run); every job Echo starts on the profile asking for one of those names asks for the mapped model (minutes, live notes, thread sync, Needs you now, prep, the Brain, routines, Yolo); a local profile's Claude Code background names too
